==PID==, parent **PPID**, owner UID, file descriptors
`ps aux` / `ps -ef` list all; `top` / `htop` live; `pgrep -f name` finds PIDs
`fork` clones the parent; `exec` swaps in a new program
==Zombie==: finished child never reaped with `wait`
==Orphan==: lost parent, adopted by **PID 1**
`kill -TERM pid` first, wait; `kill -9 pid` as a **last resort**
`cmd &` backgrounds; Ctrl+Z suspends; `bg` / `fg` resume behind / forward
`nohup` or `disown` survives logout; `nice -n 10` starts nicer; `renice` changes a running PID

slides.subtitle: Who runs, and how to stop it

items: ==stdin== 0, ==stdout== 1, ==stderr== 2 start every process
`2>&1` copies where stdout points ==right now==
`tee` writes a file and passes data on
`xargs` lines to arguments; `-0` with `-print0` survives spaces
`<<EOF` feeds multi-line input to stdin
`> f` wipes an existing file before the command runs
`2>&1 > f` leaves stderr on the terminal
A failing early stage hides without `pipefail`

blocks.note: tee runs as root; redirect doesn't

blocks.title: Interview Point
items: `cmd 2>&1 > out.txt` leaves stderr on screen: order matters
Pipeline returns last status; no `pipefail` hides failures
`sudo echo x > /etc/f` fails: redirect runs as you; tee fixes it
Key: redirects go left to right, pipes run concurrently; no `-0` splits on spaces

slides.page_title: Text Processing with grep, sed and awk

items: `grep -rnE 'err|warn' src/`: recursive, line numbers, ==extended regex==; `-i` case, `-v` **inverts**, `-c` counts, `-l` file names; `rg` is faster
`sed 's/old/new/g'` substitutes per line; `g` = all; `-n` + `p` prints **only** matches
`'/re/d'` deletes matches; `-i` edits in place; `-i.bak` keeps a ==backup==
`awk -F, '{print $1, $3}'`: split on commas, print fields 1, 3
`NR` line number; `NF` field count; `pattern {action}` filters; `END {}` runs once at end
`sed -i` with **no backup**: use `-i.bak`, then `diff` file file.bak
`s/a/b/` without `g` changes only the first match; awk's `$3` needs single quotes
